summary: U.S. markets rallied on Friday after a surprise July jobs report showed the economy unexpectedly lost 23,000 jobs while unemployment ticked down slightly to 4.1%. The weaker-than-expected labor data drove speculation that the Federal Reserve won't be forced to raise interest rates anytime soon, halting a two-day equity decline. The S&P 500 gained 0.47% while the Nasdaq climbed 0.96%, with bond yields declining five basis points to 4.63%. Bitcoin ETFs extended their strongest inflow streak of 2026, pulling in $626 million over the first three trading days of August, with BlackRock's IBIT capturing roughly $479 million. The crypto rally pushed Bitcoin above $65,000, recovering from July's heavy redemptions. Markets are now positioned for their best week since April as investors weigh whether the Fed's hawkish stance—which saw three dissents at July's meeting—will soften heading into September.

signals.title: July jobs report shows unexpected 23,000 job losses, easing Fed rate hike pressure
signals.desc: The surprise decline in payrolls lowered expectations for near-term Fed rate hikes, with money markets now pricing no hike before December, driving equities higher.

signals.title: Bitcoin ETFs record $626M inflows over three days, BlackRock's IBIT leads
signals.desc: U.S. spot Bitcoin ETFs snapped July's outflow trend with the strongest three-day streak since late July, signaling renewed institutional appetite as BTC reclaimed $65,000.

signals.title: Fed Chair Warsh faces three dissents at July FOMC meeting, most since 2016
signals.desc: Three regional Fed presidents voted for a rate hike in July, signaling vocal hawkish pressure within the committee despite the majority holding rates steady until September.

signals.title: Treasury yields decline as labor market cools, 10-year falls to 4.63%
signals.desc: Bond markets rallied on softer jobs data, with the 10-year yield down 5 basis points, though the curve remains inverted as inflation concerns linger.

signals.title: S&P 500 set for best week since April on earnings strength and rate relief
signals.desc: Equity indexes rebounded from midweek losses as 85% of reporting S&P 500 companies beat expectations, with aggregate profits tracking over 47% growth.

verdict: Markets shrug off hawkish Fed dissents as weak jobs data delays rate hike timeline, driving risk-on sentiment into month-end.
